name: Krupowki and the Centre
tagline: The main pedestrian street and everything around it
description: Zakopane's spine is a pedestrian street of restaurants, oscypek stalls, bars and shops running from the church down towards the Gubalowka funicular. Living on or just off it means everything is a two-minute walk, and it also means the crowds are outside your window every weekend of the season.
bestFor: Short stays that want the restaurants, the funicular and the bus station all on foot
pros: Every restaurant, bar and shop within a few minutes
Bus and minibus departures for the trailheads leave from here
The funicular up Gubalowka at the end of the street
cons: Genuinely crowded through the ski and summer seasons

name: Koscieliska
tagline: The old wooden street, quieter and architecturally the best
description: The historic road running west from the centre, lined with the wooden highlander houses and Witkiewicz villas that gave the Zakopane Style its name, along with the old church and the Peksowy Brzyzek cemetery. It is a genuine conservation area, ten minutes from Krupowki and considerably calmer.
bestFor: Stays that want the town's actual architecture rather than its shopping street
pros: The finest surviving Zakopane Style buildings
Ten minutes to the centre on foot
cons: Old wooden buildings vary in comfort and insulation
Coach traffic to the western valleys passes along it

name: Kuznice and the Approach
tagline: The trailhead end, at the foot of the Kasprowy cable car
description: The southern approach towards Kuznice, where the road ends at the cable car station and the main trails into the High Tatras begin. Accommodation is scattered pensions and houses on the wooded slope, and the national park boundary is right there. You walk to the mountains rather than driving.
bestFor: Anyone whose reason for being here is walking out of the door onto a trail
pros: Tatra trails and the cable car within walking distance
Best air and views in town
cons: Twenty-five minutes on foot to Krupowki
Almost no shops or restaurants nearby
Heavy day-visitor traffic to the cable car

name: Olcza
tagline: Eastern residential slopes, cheaper and lived-in
description: A residential district on the eastern side of town, away from the tourist streets, with ordinary houses, local shops and a genuine year-round population. Rents are noticeably lower than anywhere near Krupowki and the walk into the centre takes about twenty minutes downhill.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a normal neighbourhood at a rent that is not a resort rent
pros: A real neighbourhood rather than a holiday street
Views across the valley to the Tatras
cons: Twenty minutes to the centre, uphill on the way back
Steep streets that are hard work in snow

name: Koscielisko
tagline: The village along the ridge, with the best views in the valley
description: A separate village west of Zakopane strung along a sunny ridge, with open meadows, wooden houses and an uninterrupted view of the Tatra wall. It is quieter and cheaper than the town, has its own ski lifts and trailheads, and is a short bus ride or a twenty-minute drive from Krupowki.
bestFor: People who want the mountain view from the window and do not need the town daily
pros: The best uninterrupted Tatra views anywhere near town
Cheaper and far quieter than Zakopane
cons: A car or bus is necessary for most things
Nothing at all to do in the evening
